chunks: That whoever recites in the first two rak'ahs of Salat al-Layl, in each rak'ah of them, al-Hamd once and
thirty times, he finishes, and there is no sin between him and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, except that He forgives it.

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two rak'ahs being referred to in the prayer
key_terms.الْحَمْدَ: Surat al-Fatihah, recited once in each rak'ah
key_terms.ذَنْبٌ: a sin for which forgiveness is promised
key_terms.صَلَاةِ: the ritual prayer, here specifically the night prayer
key_terms.غَفَرَ: forgave; Allah's act of pardoning the worshipper
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Surat al-Ikhlas, recited thirty times in each rak'ah

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting al-Hamd and Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad in the first two rak'ahs of Salat al-Layl?
ai.summary: This hadith encourages a particular recitation in the first two rak'ahs of Salat al-Layl: al-Hamd once and Surat al-Ikhlas thirty times in each rak'ah. It describes a great spiritual reward, namely that the worshipper completes the prayer with his sins forgiven by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: thirty times in each of the first two Rak'ahs of the night prayer, he will finish his prayer without any sin remaining between him and Allah (swt), the Mighty and Glorious, except that He forgives it”.
